statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band as the cash session closes at its high and CME equity-index futures move into the weekly halt.

headline: Nasdaq-100 closes at its session high on quadruple witching as the weekly futures halt removes the tradable path
body: NDX settled at 29,644.17, up 197.19 points or 0.67%, within a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range after opening at 29,529.64. The close landed roughly four points under the session high, which in isolation is the classic holding-near-extremes signal. The decisive counterweight is the shape of the day that produced it: price sold off about 0.53% from the open to 29,371.89 and then retraced the entire move and extended. Retracements completed rather than failed, which is the opposite of the pathological no-pullback path, and the closing push coincided with a quadruple-witching expiration that concentrated settlement flow into the 20:00Z print rather than reflecting persistent directional efficiency. Volatility confirms the benign read: VIX closed at 14.82, down about 4% and near its 14.80 session low, so the protection bid decayed into the weekend. Internals conflicted rather than aligned. Megacaps finished split four up and four down, with Amazon, Alphabet and Broadcom higher against Meta, Microsoft, Apple and Tesla, while semiconductors diverged sharply as Micron gained over 3% and Broadcom 2.3% against a 5.2% decline in Qualcomm. The macro backdrop stays demanding but stopped tightening today. The Federal Reserve raised its target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September under Chair Warsh, the first hike in three years, and October hike pricing remained live into the close, leaving the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.998% after a roughly five basis point rise and a 4.971-5.008 range, against a 2-year near 4.67%. Energy moved the other way and drained an amplifier: WTI fell 2.42% to $99.44 and Brent eased 1.61% to $103.13 as the US-Iran supply premium unwound, which is the single clearest de-alignment across the cross-asset set. The structural fact that dominates the forecast is the calendar, not the tape. US cash trading has closed and CME equity-index futures close the week at 21:00 UTC. The Sunday reopen at 22:00 UTC falls outside this 24-hour horizon, so twenty-three of the twenty-four forecast slots contain no tradable price path at all. Tail is therefore scored at 16 for the current hour and falls to a residual 9-13 across the halt, a figure that represents unpriced weekend gap exposure rather than observed structure, since mean-reversion failure has no mechanism while the venue is closed. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was read for this run and was partial: breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections were available as delayed latest-session context and are consistent with the split internals described above, while the futures and calendar sections were unavailable, so all price-path, yield, volatility and crude levels here come from independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: The window opened on the Thursday evening that followed the 16 September Fed hike, carrying a trend-up mode and Tail of 20-21 that mapped to WATCH through 21:00Z. Tail decayed to 17-18 overnight as the mode normalised, then held between 15 and 19 across the Asian and European sessions with the mapped state at EA_ON for every remaining hour. The mode ran normal through the Asian hours, turned trend-up across the European morning from 07:00Z, then shifted to mixed at 11:00Z as the US session traded two-way, and stayed mixed into the close. Stress was the more active series: it fell to 40 overnight, climbed through the 40s as crude held above $100 and the 10-year pressed 5%, peaked at 51 in the early US afternoon, then eased to 47 by 19:00Z as oil turned lower. Confidence held in a tight 85-88 band throughout, reflecting continuously available price-path evidence.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries the completed cash close and roughly half an hour of thinning post-close futures trade, with Tail at 16 and a narrow flagged window to 21:00 UTC covering that liquidity drain into the weekly halt. CME equity-index futures then close for the week at 21:00Z, and because the Sunday 22:00Z reopen falls outside this horizon, the remaining twenty-three slots contain no tradable price path. Forecast Tail drops to a residual 9 and drifts slowly to 13 by the end of the window as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates, while Stress decays from 44 to a low of 22 overnight before climbing back to 30 on reopen proximity. The mapped state is EA_ON for every slot, since the pathological price path that Tail measures requires an open venue. Confidence eases from 88 to 78 across the window, tracking distance from the last observation rather than any conflict in the evidence. No scheduled US macro release falls inside this window; the next calendar item is the Chicago Fed National Activity Index on Monday at 12:30 UTC.
